key_insight: GaMO uses geometry-aware multi-view diffusion outpainting to synthesize consistent novel views from very few input images, enabling substantially better 3D reconstructions from sparse views.
problem_solved: Improves 3D reconstruction quality when only a small number of input views are available, addressing missing coverage, inconsistent geometry, and insufficient training data for dense multi-view methods.
method: Geometry-aware conditioning: incorporate camera poses, coarse depth or epipolar constraints to guide generation and enforce multi-view geometric consistency.
Multi-view diffusion outpainting: a diffusion-based model synthesizes novel, view-consistent image content beyond observed pixels across new camera poses to augment views.
Integration with reconstruction: use generated views as augmentation or direct inputs for standard multi-view fusion/NeRF pipelines to produce higher-fidelity 3D geometry.
impact: Enables reliable 3D capture from fewer photos, reducing data-collection cost and expanding applicability of reconstruction methods to in-the-wild and resource-constrained settings.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: sparse input images + camera poses → geometry-aware diffusion outpainting → augmented multi-view set → 3D reconstruction mesh.
Before/after comparison: side-by-side 3D reconstructions from sparse views with and without GaMO augmentation.
Geometry overlay: an image showing epipolar lines/depth cues guiding the diffusion outpainting to highlight geometry conditioning.
Bar chart: reconstruction quality (e.g., IoU/Chamfer) vs. number of input views, showing GaMO gains at low view counts.
paper_title: GaMO: Geometry-aware Multi-view Diffusion Outpainting for Sparse-View 3D Reconstruction
paper_authors: Yi-Chuan Huang, Hao-Jen Chien, Chin-Yang Lin, Ying-Huan Chen, Yu-Lun Liu
